title: The weight of sacred history: the Church, the world, angels, and God himself
pass_a_gloss: Weigh sacred history's weight and moment, and ask what greater matters can be imagined than those that touch not only some nation and commonwealth, but the whole Church God selected for himself from the world — nay the universal world, the angels who inhabit Heaven, and God himself, first cause of all things. Sacred Scripture's history turns on these. It tells the universe's beginnings and cradles; how God once founded all things and ordered them to exist; whence the human race was born and propagated; how it spread through the whole earth; and what at the start were the divisions of nations and tongues. It narrates angelic appearances and frequent colloquies with men, and God's admirable deeds in ruling and guarding the Church and procuring the human race's salvation. Set Greek or Roman histories beside these and nothing matches them in moment and gravity.
pass_b_english: Now if anyone wishes to weigh the weight and moment of sacred history, what matters of greater weight and moment can be imagined than those which pertain not only to some nation and commonwealth, but to the whole Church which God selected for himself out of the world — nay, to the universal world, to the angels who inhabit Heaven, and to God himself, who is the first cause of all things? These are the things about which sacred Scripture's history turns. For Scripture tells us what were this universe's beginnings and cradles, and how God once founded all things and ordered them to exist; whence the human race was born and propagated; how it spread through the whole earth; and what were at the beginning the divisions of nations and of tongues. It narrates the appearances of angelic spirits and their frequent colloquies with men, and God's own admirable deeds in ruling and guarding the Church and procuring the human race's salvation. If anyone compares Greek or Roman histories with these, he will find nothing whose moment and gravity can in any part match them.
source_text: XLI. Jam vero si quis historiae sacrae pondus et momentum perpendere velit, quae res majoris ponderis et momenti esse fingi possunt, quam quae non modo ad gentem et rempublicam aliquam pertinent, sed ad totam Ecclesiam quam Deus sibi e mundo selegit, imo ad mundum universum, ad angelos Coelorum incolas, et ad Deum ipsum, qui est prima rerum omnium causa. Haec vero sunt circa quae versatur Scripturae sacrae historia. Nam Scriptura nobis recitat quae fuerint hujus universi primordia et incunabula, et quomodo Deus olim omnia condidit et extare jussit: unde genus humanum natum et propagatum est, quomodo per totum orbem terrarum se diffudit, et quae fuerint initio divisiones gentium et linguarum. Narrat angelicorum spirituum apparitiones, et frequentia cum hominibus colloquia: Deique ipsius admiranda facta in Ecclesia regenda et tuenda, humanique generis salute procuranda. Cum quibus si quis conferat historias Graecorum sive Romanorum, nil inveniet cujus momentum et gravitas possit ulla ex parte cum hisce comparari.
